notes: drmTMB convention: larger sigma always means larger modelled variability.

scale_meaning: residual scale and degrees of freedom
notes: drmTMB uses log(nu - 2) (logm2 link) on nu so nu > 2 is enforced and the variance is finite; as nu grows, Student-t approaches Gaussian.

natural_sd_ratio: exp(beta) (multiplies the geometric mean of Y)
notes: drmTMB convention: Y > 0, log(Y) ~ Normal(mu, sigma^2); coefficients on mu live on the log-response scale, so exp(beta) is the multiplicative effect on the geometric mean of Y.
gllvmTMB Gaussian latent model: between-unit covariance is \boldsymbol{\Lambda}_B \boldsymbol{\Lambda}_B^\top + \boldsymbol{\Psi}_B; row-level residual is a single shared \sigma_\epsilon.
drmTMB convention: rho12 in (-1, 1) via an atanh_guarded link (response-scale correlation is 0.99999999 * tanh(eta_rho12)).

scale_meaning: Gamma dispersion (CV of the response is roughly sigma when sigma is small)
notes: drmTMB convention with stats::Gamma(link = "log"): Y > 0; log(mu_i) is the linear predictor on the mean; sigma_i is the dispersion (related to the shape parameter).

scale_meaning: Beta precision (larger sigma -> distribution tighter around mu)
natural_sd_ratio: exp(beta) on the precision (multiplicative); odds ratio on mu (exp(beta) on the logit scale)
notes: drmTMB Beta family: Y in (0, 1); mu_i is the mean on the response scale via the logit link; sigma_i is the precision parameter on the log scale.

scale_meaning: Poisson has no dispersion parameter; variance = mean
notes: drmTMB convention with stats::poisson(): Y in {0, 1, 2, ...}; log(mu_i) is the linear predictor; variance equals the mean.

scale_meaning: Overdispersion (small sigma -> Poisson; large sigma -> highly overdispersed)
notes: drmTMB nbinom2: Y in {0, 1, 2, ...}; mu_i is the mean count rate on the log scale; size = exp(sigma_i); variance = mu + mu^2 / exp(sigma).

scale_meaning: Precision / inverse-overdispersion (small sigma -> highly overdispersed, large sigma -> binomial limit)
natural_sd_ratio: exp(beta) on precision; odds ratio on mu
notes: drmTMB Beta-binomial: response is a count of successes out of N_i trials specified via cbind(successes, failures); mu_i is the mean success probability on the logit link; sigma_i parameterises overdispersion on the log scale.

scale_meaning: Overdispersion on the log scale (size parameter = exp(sigma))
variance_expression: Note: the modelled mean mu is the mean of the UNTRUNCATED distribution; the truncated mean is larger.
notes: drmTMB truncated_nbinom2: Y >= 1 (zeros are excluded by the likelihood); mu_i is the mean of the underlying untruncated negative binomial; sigma_i parameterises overdispersion on the log scale (size = exp(sigma_i)).

scale_meaning: The response is ordered categorical with K levels; the model has K-1 cutpoints theta_k (which replace the intercept) and a shared slope vector beta (proportional-odds assumption)
variance_expression: P(Y <= k) is the CDF on the cumulative-logit scale; the response-scale probability of being exactly in category k is P(Y <= k) - P(Y <= k-1)
natural_sd_ratio: exp(beta) is a proportional-odds ratio across all category boundaries
notes: drmTMB cumulative_logit: assumes the SAME slope vector applies to every cumulative log-odds (proportional-odds assumption). Check this before interpreting.

scale_meaning: Binary response with logit-link mean; no separate dispersion parameter
variance_expression: P(Y=1) = logit^{-1}(eta); variance Bernoulli, depends on mean
natural_sd_ratio: exp(beta) (odds ratio on the success probability)
notes: gllvmTMB Binomial latent model: each trait is Bernoulli on the logit scale; between-unit covariance is Lambda_B Lambda_B^T (+ Psi_B); no row-level residual (Bernoulli variance is determined by the mean).
